newsitem.title: USA: U.S. swap spreads creep wider on repo, stocks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. swap spreads creep wider on repo, stocks.

text.p: U.S. interest rate swap spreads widened on Friday, most notably in the 10-year area, due mainly to lower Treasury repurchase rates, traders said.

A fierce selloff in the U.S. stock market, which typically translates into wider Treasury-Eurodollar (TED) spreads, was also supporting front-end swap spreads, although the spreads acutally had come in slightly earlier in the day.
"For some reason, Eurodollars were outperforming Treasuries before three o'clock (1500 EDT/1900 GMT, when the futures markets closed)," said a dealer at a Japanese bank.
"But stocks got hit hard late in the day, so I would say front-end spreads have widened out since then," he added.

He said flight-to-quality buying of government securities usually pushed out spreads when corporate creditworthiness came under pressure. The Dow Jones Industrial average fell 247.37 points to 7,694.66 on Friday, capping its worst ever week in which it lost more than 330 points.
The trader assessed the mid-market level for the two-year swap spread at 32 basis points or slightly higher at 1700 EDT/2100 GMT.
The two-year was quoted earlier in the day at 31 bps bid/32.5 bps offered after hovering at 32/33 bps in the earlier part of the week.
The 10-year spread was pegged at 42.5/43.5 bps, up from 41/43 earlier in the week and 40/41 late last week.
Traders said tightness in the repo market was continuing to push spreads wider.
"It's been slowly creeping up," said a U.S. bank trader. "It's a function of long-term supply and demand (for Treasury notes)."
